title: Laredo wraps third Miraaa Media Fest, celebrating the river and border creativity
excerpt: Laredo has wrapped the third installment of the Miraaa Media Fest, a border film festival built around the Rio Grande, with top honors going to local filmmakers Maya López, Leann Bernal and Ryan Cerna.
content:
Laredo has concluded the third installment of the Miraaa Media Fest, an experimental film festival created by border artists that this year took the Rio Grande itself as its theme, according to Tragaluz.

The festival began in 2021 as a fully virtual event focused on the Rio Grande Valley, organized by Entre Film Center and Trucha RGV. In its second year, the Laredo Film Society and the Daphne Art Foundation joined to add Laredo as a venue. This year, the festival expanded hundreds of miles upriver and added Eagle Pass as a third venue.

In Laredo, the Featured Short award went to “Despues de la Luz,” a film by former Vidal M. Treviño School of Communications and Fine Arts student Maya López, now at the University of Texas at Austin. The movie was filmed at Casa Ortiz and follows a quinceañera that is violently interrupted by an immigration raid, presenting what the festival described as a portrait of modern life on the Texas border.

The commissioned artist award went to “Plaza Eterna,” a collaboration between dancer Leann Bernal and editor Ryan Cerna, with an original score by Miro Santos. The film is set to the story of a “flooded” Plaza Theater, recalling the downtown theater’s golden age after it opened in the 1950s and the much earlier history of the river’s first stewards.

Bernal said she was grateful for the chance to create as a border artist in an experimental festival, where there is no right or wrong, and described the work as something to feel, like the river. A panel discussion during the festival featured Seyde García, Tricia Cortez of the Rio Grande International Study Center, RGISC board president Margarita Araiza, environmentalist and biologist Dr. Amede Rubio, and RGISC neighborhood cultural organizer Mario Flores.

Source: Tragaluz, November 5, 2026.
